heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v25's algorithm (v22's with P's certified output read as advice; proof Z.1) outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of the pre-registered study R7 are an unselected sample of v20's (equally v22's and v25's) runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws.
heuristics.scope: R5N (proof R.1, R.3): m2 keeps tentative entries as update logs and algorithm() keeps each accepted space's basis; on any coins the outputs, coins and WK counters equal 0f72a85e's (v25's) unless B_TRUE, which now also counts the rebuild extras (at most 1.0025 x the old true cost), acts where it did not; in R7 only runs 10 (2^28.39) and 32 (2^28.60) have old true cost above 2^27.998 units, and both are counted as failures: 37 of 48, one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound 0.6493 >= 0.40. Only the success probability. Each R7 run is a complete run of v20 with label-derived coins (proof W.2): r7run.py makes algorithm()'s calls in algorithm()'s order from r5v20.py, which is v19's experiment file with K_SPACES = 50, A_ADV = 1067, A_MAX = 4268 and S2CAP = 2^11 (and an R5-replay bound written as 96); the shipped r5.py differs from it only in trail_search's loop order (W.4: same output, Lemma W; R7 uses P's certified output, as R5 and R6 did), in the organizer replay tables (W.10) and in the spacing of ten constant tables (AST-checked) and in R5N4's one statement `cs = None` in bprime, which frees the previous candidate's setup before the next is built and changes no value, coin or counter; v22's r5.py differs from v20's only in the counted programs and their checks (X), which algorithm() never calls, and in whitespace outside algorithm()'s call graph; v22's algorithm() and every definition it reaches are byte-identical to v20's (X.10, X.11); v25's algorithm() starts from P's certified output, exactly as every R7 run did, and by AST differs from v22's only there (Z.1); v25's counted programs (Z.2, Z.3) are not called by algorithm(). E on a space is fes (exact stage 1, Lemma 4, self-checked at 64 checkpoints) and stage 2 by complete digests in fes's order on at most S2CAP passes, which changes at most which colliding pair of a space is output. In R7, B_BUDGET, B_TRUE, X_MAX, A_MAX and S2CAP never acted: largest attempt 197,334 work units (X_MAX 2^20), stage-2 counts 199-310 (S2CAP 2^11), true B' cost at most 2^28.60 units (B_TRUE 2^29), at most 1,201 attempts in a run (A_MAX 4268); CCAP and A_ADV acted only as the algorithm prescribes (per-run table, W.2). Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R7: 39 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.6956, so by R7's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported. Premise R: rule K, R7's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, experiment file and enumerator were hashed at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof W.2, Appendix F: per-run table and ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; which runs the organizer replays and which collisions are certificates was fixed before any result existed. The model that chose K predicts p_50 = 0.739; R7 measures the algorithm itself. Premise P is not used: the trail is advice whose construction is R.8's capped runs, charged in Appendix M (Z.1); the organizer still re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R7: r5-R-0..7 re-derive 8 seed-picked R7 successes per review (one per stratum; v25s, Z.6) from their labels; r5-bpfull re-runs a whole B' of an R7 run; the first 15 R7 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R7's failures, run order and timing are logged by us. The organizer re-derives 8 of R7's 39 successes per review (one per stratum; v25s, Z.6) (run 22 only in the per-run ledger); failures are not re-run. Rule K was written after G2, C, D, C', R5 and R6 had run, with their outcomes known (proof W.1); R7 ran after rule K and its plan were hashed. R5 and R6 (K = 96) are not runs of v20. The advice's full-scale certification rests on R.8's capped runs (s12, 133.8 s, one core; v15's native run of 296 CPU-s reproduced its counts), charged in Appendix M; the organizer checks the output core and seed-picked cores per review at the certifying level; success does not depend on it (Z.1).
